repo.description:
### Summary

The sign-up endpoint answered differently depending on whether an email address already had an account, letting an unauthenticated caller test addresses.

### Details

`signup` in `users.service.ts`, and its Enterprise override, rejected an address that already had an account with a message saying the user already exists. The Enterprise version also answered an address with a pending invitation with a message saying it had already been invited. On an instance with open signup, an unregistered address simply creates an account. With invite-only signup turned on, an unregistered address was refused by `registerNewUserIfAllowed` with a different message and no account was created, so the two answers told registered and unregistered addresses apart without leaving anything behind. Sign-up now gives one answer for every address that already has an account, registered or invited, and with invite-only signup on, registered and unregistered addresses receive the same answer.

### Impact

No authentication is required. An attacker could learn whether an email address has an account on the instance and, where the Enterprise sign-up is in use, whether it has a pending invitation. On instances with invite-only signup this needed no account to be created. No account data or credentials were exposed.

### Credit

This issue was reported by [@NinjaGPT](https://github.com/NinjaGPT).
